newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's alumina plant closure becomes open-ended.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's alumina plant closure becomes open-ended.

text.p: Hungary's second-biggest alumina plant, HungAlumina Kft's Almasfuzitoi Timfoldgyar, extended its one-week closure for an as-yet undefined period, the factory's chief executive said on Monday.
"The closure is now open-ended," Pal Havas told Reuters in a telephone interview from this northwestern Hungarian town.
Almasfuzito closed last week for one week, which Havas said was due to the factories' production becoming uneconomical due to falling international alumina prices.
Newspapers reported last week that HungAlumina was looking for banks to help finance further production, on which Havas declined to comment.
Almasfuzito produced about 140,000 tonnes of alumina last year, roughly two-thirds of which was smelter-grade.
The smelter-grade alumina was sold partly in Romania, but mainly to smelters in Russia's distant Ural region, which were reluctant to buy alumina above $200 a tonne cif, Havas said.
With transportation costs amounting to $70 a tonne, such sales are uneconomical, he explained.
Almasfuzito was once part of Hungary's state-owned aluminium producer Hungalu Rt, which closed it in 1994 for lack of markets.
Last year, however, HungAlumina, a joint venture between Germany's ALFER Holding GmbH, Britain's Alucan Metals Corp and Hungary's Metalservice Kft, reopened the plant.
